text:
A model's last layer gives every token in its vocabulary a score, called a logit. Something still has to pick one. Say the sentence so far is, her new pet is a. Cat scores three point two... and rock scores minus zero point four. Softmax turns scores into probabilities. It raises e to each score, then divides by the total. Cat gets sixty-five percent, three times dog's share from a gap of one point one. Rock gets under two. And the picking isn't done by the model. It's a few lines of code with a couple of settings... and it's why one prompt can give different answers.

Temperature divides every score before the softmax. The order never changes... only the shape does. Below one, the gaps grow. At zero point two, cat takes over ninety-nine percent. At zero, it takes the top token every time. That's greedy decoding. Above one, the gaps shrink. At one point five, rock climbs to almost five percent.

Top p trims the tail before the draw. Keep the likeliest tokens until they cover ninety percent, and drop the rest. At one point five, that keeps cat, dog and bird. Rock can't be drawn at all. And the cut adapts. When the model's sure, one token covers ninety percent on its own. When it's torn between six, all six stay in.

Still, every pick is a draw. Five runs over the same three close scores give five different strings. In a real model, each pick becomes context for the next, so two answers can agree for a sentence and then split completely. And the sampler always picks something, even when nothing true is on the list.
